_comment: Demo video script. Sources: A = full walkthrough recording, B = explorer + workspace tour. Times in seconds. Each line is [spoken text for the voice, caption text]. Spoken text uses phonetic spellings (Forge, Q I E, main net).

lines: Shipping a smart contract usually means juggling compilers, scripts, R.P.C. settings, wallets and spreadsheets.
Shipping a smart contract usually means juggling compilers, scripts, RPC settings, wallets and spreadsheets.
Forge puts that whole release process into one workspace, built for Q I E Blockchain.
4ORGE puts that whole release process into one workspace, built for QIE Blockchain.
Sign in with email or GitHub, and you get your own private workspace.
Sign in with email or GitHub, and you get your own private workspace.
Next, connect a wallet. Here it's Rabby, on Q I E main net.
Next, connect a wallet. Here it's Rabby, on QIE Mainnet.
Forge never asks for a seed phrase or a private key. Your wallet stays in control.
4ORGE never asks for a seed phrase or a private key. Your wallet stays in control.
Let's bring in a real project: atlas pad, a Foundry monorepo, straight from GitHub.
Let's bring in a real project: atlaspad, a Foundry monorepo, straight from GitHub.
Forge streams the repository and reads its config files as text. It never runs them.
4ORGE streams the repository and reads its config files as text. It never runs them.
Even big repositories are fine: only Solidity, test and config files are kept.
Even big repositories are fine: only Solidity, test and config files are kept.
It finds every contract, test and dependency, and picks up the compiler settings from foundry dot toml.
It finds every contract, test and dependency, and picks up the compiler settings from foundry.toml:
Solidity zero point eight point twenty-eight, optimizer on, Cancun.
Solidity 0.8.28, optimizer on, Cancun.
Now, start a deployment. Pick the contract, Atlas Governor, and fill in its constructor arguments.
Now, start a deployment. Pick the contract, AtlasGovernor, and fill in its constructor arguments.
They're type-checked against the A.B.I. as you type, and address fields also accept Q I E I D names.
They're type-checked against the ABI as you type, and address fields also accept QIE ID names.
Then choose Q I E main net, and start.
Then choose QIE Mainnet, and start.
Forge saves this as a Runbook, and runs it step by step.
4ORGE saves this as a Runbook, and runs it step by step.
It verifies the chain I D, compiles with the official Solidity compiler, and runs all one hundred and fourteen tests in a sandbox.
It verifies the chain ID, compiles with the official Solidity compiler, and runs all 114 tests in a sandbox.
Every step is logged on the right, so you can see exactly what happened, and when.
Every step is logged on the right, so you can see exactly what happened, and when.
If a single test fails, nothing gets deployed.
If a single test fails, nothing gets deployed.
Then it stops for the two things only you can do. First, review: the contract, network, deployer, arguments and maximum gas cost.
Then it stops for the two things only you can do. First, review: the contract, network, deployer, arguments and maximum gas cost.
Because this is main net, you have to type main net to continue.
Because this is Mainnet, you have to type MAINNET to continue.
Second, sign. Rabby shows its own confirmation, and nothing is sent until you approve it there.
Second, sign. Rabby shows its own confirmation, and nothing is sent until you approve it there.
Then Q I E confirms the transaction.
Then QIE confirms the transaction.
Forge doesn't just trust a transaction hash. It reads the receipt back from the chain, and checks the sender, the exact bytecode, and the status.
4ORGE doesn't just trust a transaction hash. It reads the receipt back from the chain, and checks the sender, the exact bytecode, and the status.
Then it records the deployment, and verifies the source code on Q I E's explorer.
Then it records the deployment, and verifies the source code on QIE's explorer.
And here it is, on the Q I E main net explorer.
And here it is, on the QIE Mainnet explorer.
The transaction succeeded, and the Atlas Governor contract is live.
The transaction succeeded, and the AtlasGovernor contract is live.
Its source code is verified too, so anyone can read exactly what was deployed.
Its source code is verified too, so anyone can read exactly what was deployed.
Everything stays tracked: your dashboard, Runbooks you can run again, a permanent deployment history, every contract, and live network health.

Projects, Runbooks and deployments all link back to the chain, so your team always knows what's live, and where.
